Title: Diana's brother compares media treatment of Harry, Meghan to late princess' ordeal
Article:
Reuters
LONDON: The media's treatment of Prince Harry and his wife Meghan is on a par with that faced by his mother Diana, the late princess' brother said in an interview published on Sunday, warning that lessons needed to be learned from that period.
Diana died aged 36 in a 1997 Paris car crash as photographers pursued her on motorbikes, sparking an outpouring of grief and a reckoning over whether the media bore some responsibility for her death after splashing details of her life across front pages for years.
"If you look at an article in a tabloid about Diana or the couple that you were mentioning, Harry and Meghan, you know, they can be really, really unpleasant," Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, told the BBC.
"And I think it would be really beholden on people to learn from Diana's example.
"I'm not here to speak for Harry and Meghan, but for anyone who's being destroyed in this way daily, it must be such a cancerous influence in their life."
Harry, Diana's youngest son, and Meghan, cited the impact of what they called a toxic media on their lives before they quit royal duties and moved to the United States in 2020.
They also sued much of the British tabloid press - with varying degrees of success - before they moved back to Britain in August.
Spencer has made headlines around the world in the last week after his book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister", was serialised in the Daily Mail, accusing her former husband, the now King Charles, of sounding "giddily elated" in the hours after her death.
The palace hit back by saying the king "is mindful that the pain of ​fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour ​memory in ⁠ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."
The publication of the book and the return of Harry and Meghan to Britain are another challenge for the king, who is still undergoing treatment for cancer.
Diana's family accused the royals of showing a lack of support or care towards the late princess before her death, a charge that was repeated by Harry, who is now largely estranged from the rest of the royal family.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia rescue agency recovers another victim from capsized ship
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's search and rescue agency said on Sunday it had recovered one more victim from the wreck of a passenger ship that capsized and sank in the Java Sea last weekend.
The passenger ship, Virgo Transport 8, was carrying 243 people, including 30 crew members, when it capsized in bad weather early on Sept 13 during a voyage from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.
"The victim was found by divers during a search inside the ship's hull," the agency said, adding that the victim will be airlifted out for identification.
The search and evacuation operation will be continued using divers and also air support, the agency said.
As of Saturday, authorities said nine people had been confirmed dead and more than 100 people had survived, leaving 126 unaccounted for.
The recovery operation for the sunken ship was extended by another week due to the number of missing people and because the salvage operation to right the ship is expected to take time, authorities said on Saturday.

Title: Najib house arrest decision first of its kind in Malaysia, says lawyer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest is the first case of its kind in Malaysia, says a prominent lawyer.
Datuk N Sivananthan, the first Malaysian lawyer admitted to the International Criminal Court (ICC), said that in his experience, prisoners had previously been transferred from prison to alternative locations strictly on health grounds.
However, he said the current situation differs because the Pardons Board's decision specifically involves serving the remaining sentence under house arrest.
Sivananthan said the implementation of the decision raises key operational questions, particularly regarding the monitoring mechanism and who will oversee Najib throughout his house arrest.
"Similarly, questions remain on whether officers will be stationed at the residence, as well as the rules governing the entry and exit of visitors.
"All these matters must be determined based on directives and procedures to be established by the Prisons Department," he said.
The 64th Pardons Board Meeting for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, and Putrajaya convened at Istana Negara on Sept 18.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who chaired the meeting, granted a conditional pardon allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and other set conditions.
Commenting on the payment procedure, Sivananthan said the fine must be paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, as the original penalty was ordered by that court following Najib's conviction on seven charges of criminal breach of trust, abuse of position, and money laundering involving RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd (SRC).
He said fine payments are typically made online via bank transfer to a court-designated account, eliminating the need for physical attendance at the Court Registry.
Once received, the bank verifies the transaction, and the receipt or proof of payment must be submitted to the court and the Prisons Department.
He added that no specific timeframe is fixed for the process, as it depends on payment processing and verification by the court.
"House arrest cannot commence until the fine is fully paid. Once the RM50 million sum is received and verified, the court will make the necessary arrangements and issue a receipt to be presented to the Prisons Department," he said.
From a legal standpoint, Sivananthan noted that Section 283 of the Criminal Procedure Code governs court authority regarding fine execution and payment procedures.
He said Najib must comply with the set fine conditions, as failure to do so would breach the conditional pardon terms, requiring him to serve out his sentence in prison.
Najib has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction in the SRC International case.
On July 28, 2020, the Kuala Lumpur High Court sentenced him to 12 years' imprisonment and a RM210 million fine after finding him guilty on seven charges, a decision subsequently upheld on appeal.
Najib submitted a petition for pardon on Sept 2, 2022. In 2024, the Pardons Board reduced his prison sentence to six years and the fine to RM50 million, setting his release date for Aug 23, 2028, subject to set conditions.

Title: 15 motorcyclists arrested for reckless riding on Lekas
Article:
KAJANG: Police arrested 15 motorcyclists for reckless and dangerous riding during an operation targeting illegal street racing along the Kajang-Seremban Expressway (Lekas) early today.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the five-hour Op Samseng Jalanan began at 12.01am.
He said police inspected 90 people and 70 motorcycles during the operation.
"A total of 15 motorcyclists were arrested under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous riding.
"Police also seized 34 motorcycles and issued 95 summonses for various traffic offences," he said in a statement today.
Naazron said a first conviction under Section 42(1) carried a jail term of up to 5 years and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM15,000.
"For a second or subsequent conviction, offenders face imprisonment of up to 10 years and a fine of between RM10,000 and RM20,000," he said.
Naazron said police would take action against anyone found riding or driving recklessly and endangering other road users.
"The public is advised to obey traffic laws and respect other road users," he said.

Title: China's August oil imports from Russia rise as Middle East flows slump
Article:
BEIJING: China's crude oil imports from Russia stood at 11.2 million metric tons in August, or 2.64 million barrels per day (bpd), up 41 per cent from a year earlier and 23 per cent from July.
Imports from Malaysia, the largest transshipment hub for sanctioned Iranian oil, reached 2.6 million tons, or 620,000 bpd, down 45 per cent year on year but up 74 per cent from July.
Imports from Indonesia stood at 3.1 million tons, or 730,000 bpd, up 16 per cent year on year and flat with July.
China imported about 100,000 tons of crude from Indonesia in all of 2024, but monthly imports first exceeded 2 million tons in July 2025.
Reuters has previously reported that the surge in imports from Indonesia could reflect efforts to disguise shipments of sanctioned Iranian crude transshipped in waters off Malaysia.
Imports from Iraq stood at 1.4 million tons, down 75 per cent from a year earlier, while imports from Oman reached 900,000 tons, down 71 per cent year-on-year, after China recorded no shipments from the country in July.
Imports from the Saudi Arabia stood at 3.2 million tons, or 740,000 bpd, down 47 per cent year on year and down 41 per cent from July.
Imports from the United Arab Emirates stood at 2.9 million tons, or 680,000 bpd, down four per cent year on year but up 20 per cent from July.
Customs data showed no crude imports from the United States, Venezuela or Iran in August, in line with the prior year.

Title: Najib touched by RM50mil fund support, says daughter
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Daddy really did not expect so many people to be willing to contribute," Nooryana Najwa said, quoting her father, Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who was touched by efforts to raise the
RM50 million fine
through the Solidarity Fund to allow him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Nooryana, popularly known as Yana Najib, said her father expressed how touched he was when she and her family visited the former prime minister at Kajang Prison yesterday.
She said the former prime minister repeatedly expressed how touched he was to see people willing to contribute towards the effort.
"Daddy really did not expect so many people to be willing to contribute. I would never force it on anyone," she said in a statement on Facebook today.
Nooryana, who is also Umno Puteri information chief, said her father had yet to be allowed to return home as the Pardons Board's decision stipulated that the RM50 million fine must first be paid.
She said the family fully respected the decision and that further arrangements would be made through official channels if the fine was successfully raised through voluntary contributions to the Solidarity Fund set up by Umno.
"Yana understands that the fine must first be paid to the court. The court will then issue a payment receipt, which will be handed to the prison authorities.
"Only then can the prison authorities issue instructions for the house arrest process," she said.
Nooryana said her family was also deeply touched by Umno's efforts to lead the Solidarity Fund, but that her father had never wanted to burden the party or the people.
She said all contributions were voluntary and based on each person's means, with no one being forced or obliged to contribute.
Nooryana also expressed her appreciation to everyone who had asked about Najib and the family's well-being and prayed for their welfare.
"May Allah repay each of you for your prayers and kindness," she said.
Last Friday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia granted Najib a conditional pardon to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to settlement of the RM50 million fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: National Welfare Foundation aid presented to family of late flight nurse Debra Moset
Article:
KUCHING: The National Welfare Foundation (YKN) has presented immediate disaster relief aid to the family of the late Debra Moset, a flight nurse who died in a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8.
The aid was presented by Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri during a visit to the family's home in Kampung Semadang, Padawan, today.
Nancy, who is also the foundation's Board of Trustees chairman, said the assistance was a gesture of concern and support for the family following their sudden loss.
"This aid cannot replace a life lost, but I hope it helps ease the family's burden during this extremely difficult period.
"Peka YKN assistance is an early form of support for victims' families. In times like these, our presence and attention are important so that grieving families do not feel alone," she said.
The immediate relief aid was handed over to Debra's husband, John Then.
Also present were Puncak Borneo member of parliament Datuk Willie Mongin, YKN chief executive officer Nordina Haron and Women, Family and Community Development Ministry deputy secretary-general (Policy) Mohd Daud Mohd Arif.
Nancy said Debra's service and sacrifice in providing healthcare to rural communities would always be remembered.
She said Debra's mother, Renog Rasas, 71, would receive the Senior Citizens Assistance beginning next month, as well as the Kenyalang Gold Card and Senior Citizen Health Benefit.
Meanwhile, on Sept 18, Women, Family and Community Development Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Maziah Che Yusoff visited the family of the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin in Kampung Baung, Pengkalan Chepa, Kota Baru, Kelantan, to present PEKA YKN assistance.
Similar assistance has also been arranged for the families of three other crash victims — the late Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham in Senawang, Negri Sembilan, and the late Alexson Adit Henry and Jessie Paya Jok in Miri.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sungai Gurun breaches danger level, flash floods hit 2 villages
Article:
YAN: Sungai Gurun in Kampung Perupok here breached the danger level following more than two hours of heavy rain today.
According to the Department of Irrigation and Drainage's (JPS) Infobanjir website, the river's water level had risen to 4.43m, exceeding the danger level of 3.5m.
The rise in water levels caused flash floods in Kampung Teroi Bukit and Kampung Titi Teras following the overflow of the river.
Yan Civil Defence District Officer Lieutenant (PA) Zul Izzi Zulkifli said 11 houses in Kampung Teroi Bukit and eight in Kampung Titi Teras had been affected by floodwaters so far.
He said no temporary evacuation centre (PPS) had been opened in the areas as of now.
"Residents are advised to remain alert to the flood early warning system," he said when contacted today.
Zul Izzi also advised residents to be prepared to evacuate if the river's water level continued to rise.
He said his personnel were currently monitoring several areas in the district at risk of flooding.

Title: Trial begins for 14 men in Kelantan cross-dressing case
Article:
KOTA BARU: The trial of 14 men accused of wearing women's clothing and acting like women began here today, with an enforcement officer taking the stand.
Lawyer Muhammad Syarafi Mohd Salleh said four enforcement officers involved in the operation were expected to testify.
"The prosecution started presenting its case today, and one witness was called.
"We were informed that four enforcement officers are expected to testify," he told reporters after the proceedings.
Syarafi said his clients had cooperated throughout the case and were later released on RM1,000 bail each with one surety.
Earlier, Lower Syariah Court judge Wan Firdaus Wan Ibrahim set Jan 24 next year for the trial to resume, allowing both sides to complete several outstanding documents.
The 14 men were charged at the same court in December last year with wearing women's clothing and shoes and acting like women at the multipurpose hall of Troika Residency, Jalan Sultan Ibrahim, at 11pm on May 30, 2025.
They pleaded not guilty and were charged under Section 19(1) of the Syariah Criminal Code (I) Enactment 2019, which covers the offence of men acting like women.

Title: North Korea fires ballistic missile off east coast, Seoul says
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea launched a ballistic missile off its eastern coast on Sunday, its second test in roughly a week and days after Pyongyang accused the US of driving tensions on the Korean Peninsula through a series of military drills.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the test firing from the Wonsan area around 3pm (0600 GMT), identifying the weapon as a ballistic missile.
Japan's defence ministry also said it appeared to be a ballistic missile.
Japanese public broadcaster NHK said the projectile had come down outside Japan's exclusive economic zone.
South Korea's National Security Council condemned the short-range missile launch, which follows a test on Sept 12.
The council urged Pyongyang to immediately cease missile activity, warning that the test directly violated UN Security Council resolutions.
On Saturday, North Korea dismissed a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog against Pyongyang's nuclear programme.
Pyongyang last week also condemned a US-led naval drill which included South Korea and Japan and which ran from Aug 29 to Sept 10 near Guam.
North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, on Friday blamed US-led military drills for "ever-worsening" tensions on the Korean Peninsula and vowed no change in the country's course to strengthen its nuclear arsenal.

Title: OSA shields Pardons Board minutes, expert warns against public disclosure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Matters discussed by the Pardons Board, including its meeting minutes, are subject to the Official Secrets Act (OSA) 1972 and cannot be disclosed publicly while classified, constitutional expert Prof Dr Nik Ahmad Kamal Nik Mahmood said.
He said documents or information classified under the OSA could be declassified if there was a need for them to be presented in court or in connection with a police investigation.
He cited the Addendum Order involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which
was previously brought before the court, as an example.
Nik Ahmad Kamal said there could be several negative implications if information from Pardons Board meetings was disclosed.
He said such disclosure could trigger controversy and affect the institution of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, while also restricting Board members from discussing applications candidly.
"To the best of my knowledge, discussions within the Pardons Board have never been made public, let alone its meeting minutes.
"Both the facts and the minutes are subject to the OSA. Therefore, on this basis, disclosure will not take place.
"However, the power lies with the Minister, as provided for under Section 2C of the OSA. It is up to the Minister and the government to decide," he said when contacted today.
Yesterday, Wanita DAP called on the government to disclose the official minutes of the Pardons Board meeting concerning the conditional pardon granted to Najib, which was decided last Friday.
Its chief,
Teo Nie Ching
, said such a significant decision could not have been made arbitrarily and called for full transparency over the process.
Section 2C of the OSA provides for the reclassification or declassification of official secrets by a Minister or public officer.
This includes a Minister responsible for a ministry, a public officer entrusted with duties relating to the ministry, department or relevant public service, as well as a Menteri Besar or Chief Minister of a state and the chief officer or head of administration responsible for state affairs.
Under the provision, a document, information or material previously classified as an official secret — whether Top Secret, Secret, Confidential or Restricted — may have its classification changed so that it is no longer considered an official secret and can be made public.
Nik Ahmad Kamal, who is also Governance, Legal and Management Cluster head at the National Council of Professors (MPN), said the prerogative powers of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan, Raja and Yang di-Pertuan Negeri in matters concerning pardons were clear.
He said disclosure could undermine the uniqueness of those prerogative powers in the country's system of governance.
"Every secret or confidential matter under the OSA can be disclosed in accordance with the provisions of the Act. There is a lifespan for some secrets, but certain information will not be disclosed because of national security and related factors.
"Can the case involving Datuk Seri Najib be treated as an exception? I do not think so because, as with previous pardon cases, there is no reason for it to be disclosed.
"Arguments such as transparency are difficult to use as a basis for disclosure in the context of the OSA," he said.
Last Friday, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consented to a conditional pardon for Najib, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, if he paid a RM50 million fine.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department (BHEUU) said in a statement that the decision was made following the consent of Sultan Ibrahim, who chaired the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting on the same day.
BHEUU said Najib must comply with the conditions imposed and that if he failed to comply with any of them, the conditional pardon would be revoked and he would have to immediately continue serving the remainder of his sentence in prison.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mass drone barrage on Moscow kills two
Article:
MOSCOW: Hundreds of drones targeting Moscow and its surrounding region killed at least two people and damaged a major refinery on the final day of Russia's parliamentary elections, the authorities said Sunday.
The capital's Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted and shot down, 450 of which were aimed at Moscow.
He accused Ukraine of attempting to interfere with a tightly controlled three-day election that is set to tighten President Vladimir Putin's 26-year grip on power.
"The unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections. The enemy did not succeed," he said on Telegram.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised the strikes, saying: "Our long-range responses had a very significant impact in the Moscow region last night."
"One of Russia's key oil industry facilities and the aggressor's logistics facility were hit. These are billions of dollars that sustain the war machine," he posted on X.
Moscow regional Governor Andrey Vorobyov said on the social media platform that at least two people were killed – a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man – in two separate locations.
A fire triggered by a drone crashing into a 21-storey building also led to 400 people being evacuated, Vorobyov said. He did not specify the drones' origin.
The attacks come at a time when Kyiv stepped up its long-range drone strike campaign against Russia in recent months, particularly against energy infrastructure to target a vital source of the Kremlin's revenue to fund its war effort, now in its fifth year.
"A facility on the territory of the Moscow Oil Refinery has been damaged, Sobyanin added, noting that no casualties had been reported so far and that emergency services were on the scene.
This major refinery has already been hit by Ukrainian strikes in recent months.
The latest strike comes after US President Donald Trump said Monday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to target each other's energy facilities.
It also comes after Russians began voting on Friday in the country's first parliamentary election since Moscow sent troops to Ukraine in February 2022, setting off a conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands.
Only parties that support Putin and the Kremlin's military campaign have been registered to run. Moscow has also organised voting in occupied Ukraine.
While few Russians doubt Putin's United Russia party will cruise to victory again, the vote offers a gauge of public support for the war.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 220 flood victims evacuated to three relief centres in Gua Musang
Article:
GUA MUSANG: A total of 220 flood victims from 56 families have been evacuated to three temporary relief centres (PPS) in Gua Musang following heavy rain.
According to the Social Welfare Department Info Banjir portal, 144 victims were housed at the Masjid Jeram Tekoh PPS, 39 at the Dewan Orang Ramai Zon 3 Jeram Tekoh, and 37 at SK Jeram Tekoh.
A fourth relief centre at the Felda Chiku 6 Community Hall has been opened but has yet to receive any evacuees.
Meanwhile, Nenggiri assemblyman Mohd Azmawi Fikri Abdul Ghani said heavy rainfall yesterday affected more than 200 homes across several areas.
[[nid:1536983]]
Flash floods hit Rancangan Kemajuan Tanah (RKT) Jeram Tekoh, RKT Sungai Asap, RKT Renok, Kampung Limau Kasturi, Kampung Serian, Batu 11 and 12, as well as Kampung Jelekang.
"Water levels rose rapidly. Some victims unable to save their belongings," he said.

Title: Former Bongawan assemblyman Karim Bujang dies at 73
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Former Bongawan assemblyman Datuk Karim Bujang died at his residence in Kampung Sipanggil, Putatan, at noon today. He was 73.
The news was confirmed by former Pantai Manis assemblyman and former Sabah Law and Native Affairs Minister Datuk Aidi Moktar.
Karim served as Bongawan assemblyman for five terms from 1990 to 2013.
During his tenure as an elected representative, he served as an assistant minister in the Sabah Cabinet, holding portfolios including finance as well as tourism, culture, and environment.
Karim later continued his political career with Parti Warisan Sabah and contested the Kimanis parliamentary seat in the 14th General Election (GE14) in 2018.
He also stood as Warisan's candidate for the Kimanis parliamentary by-election in 2020.

Title: 43,000 litres of subsidised diesel seized, three held in Perak raid
Article:
IPOH: The Perak Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry detained three men and seized 43,000 litres of subsidised diesel during a raid at a fishing jetty in Hutan Melintang, near Teluk Intan, yesterday.
Perak ministry director Datuk Kamalludin Ismail said the 5am raid under Ops Tiris 4.0 also led to the seizure of a Class C fishing boat, a tanker lorry, two skid tanks, hoses, oil transfer equipment, a hydraulic electric pump, and several related documents.
"The total value of the seizure is estimated at RM1,525,190. The case is being investigated under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 and the Control of Supplies Regulations 1974," he said in a statement today.
He said the three local suspects, aged between 33 and 42, comprised the tanker lorry driver, an attendant, and the jetty owner.
"Initial investigations found that the fishermen's diesel, purchased at RM1.65 per litre, was believed to have been resold on the black market at nearly RM4 per litre," he said.
Kamalludin said intelligence gathered revealed that the tanker lorry entered the jetty to collect diesel stored in two skid tanks.
He said both tanks were believed to contain fishermen's diesel siphoned and transferred without authorisation from a Class C fishing boat belonging to the jetty owner.
"An inspection found that diesel was being transferred without valid authorisation under the Control of Supplies Act 1961, alongside suspected diversion of subsidised fishermen's diesel," he said.
He added that upon conviction, individuals face fines of up to RM1 million, imprisonment of up to three years, or both, while corporate entities face fines of up to RM2 million for a first offence and up to RM5 million for subsequent offences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH-Bersatu pact can work, but trust, voter support crucial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An electoral pact between former allies Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu could work in Melaka, but its success will depend on rebuilding trust and broadening voter support, political analysts say.
Bersatu was part of PH's winning coalition in the 14th General Election in 2018, but its withdrawal during the Sheraton Move in 2020 brought down the PH government.
Universiti Malaya senior lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said cooperation could help PH expand its Malay support, but Bersatu would have to demonstrate its electoral strength before seeking seats.
"Bersatu can bring genuine electoral value in particular Malay-majority seats, but it cannot simply expect seats.
"It will need to demonstrate local machinery, credible candidates and the ability to attract votes that PH cannot easily secure on its own," he told the New Straits Times.
He said winnability should take precedence over party entitlement, with PH having to balance the interests of PKR, DAP and Amanah against the potential gains from accommodating Bersatu.
"In a close state election, even a limited shift in Malay support, local machinery or candidate appeal can affect several seats," he said.
Tawfik said memories of the Sheraton Move could make PH supporters wary of the arrangement, requiring clear commitments and safeguards to rebuild confidence.
"The partnership needs a clear common agenda, credible candidates and an explanation that reassures PH's existing supporters. Otherwise, PH Plus may be seen as an opportunistic arrangement rather than a convincing political alternative."
International Islamic University Malaysia political analyst Dr Syaza Shukri said the parties' relatively distinct voter bases offered room for an electoral pact to avoid three-cornered fights without Bersatu formally rejoining PH.
However, she said distrust remained a stumbling block for both PH voters and its leadership, which wanted assurances that Bersatu would not turn against the coalition again.
Syaza said PH's completed seat distribution meant PKR and Amanah might have to give up some allocations to accommodate Bersatu, with winnability again being the deciding factor.
However, she questioned how much additional support Bersatu could deliver.
"Bersatu has grassroots in Melaka but they may have switched to Wawasan following their leaders. And without that, I'm not sure how much Bersatu can help PH."
Meanwhile, Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Prof Dr Azizudin Md Sani said cooperation was realistic as Bersatu sought partners to help it win seats and retain the two it secured in the previous state election.
He said PH Plus could involve Bersatu and other parties willing to make a common commitment, although the proposed arrangement remained unclear.
"PH will share seats with Bersatu if such collaboration is agreed upon," he said, adding that seeking other partners could strengthen PH's electoral position.
Yesterday, Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition was finalising negotiations with parties sharing similar aspirations, including Bersatu,
to form a PH Plus
collaboration for the state election, in line with decisions by the PH Presidential Council.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration detains 15 foreigners in Pandan Jaya illegal gambling raids
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department detained 15 foreigners following raids on four premises allegedly used for illegal gambling in Pandan Jaya.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the special operation was conducted at four locations shortly after midnight on Sept 19 by officers from the Intelligence and Special Operations Division at the department's Putrajaya headquarters.
He said the raids followed a month of intelligence gathering based on public information.
"During the operation, we detained a Bangladeshi man and an Indonesian woman believed to be the premises' caretaker and cashier, respectively.
"Also detained were three Myanmar men, two Indonesian men, a Bangladeshi man, an Indian man and six Indonesian women," he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said all 15 foreigners, aged between 21 and 38, were suspected of immigration offences, including misusing their passes, overstaying and not possessing valid travel documents or passes.
Authorities also seized seven Indonesian passports, 31 tablets, 15 mobile phones, a workers' schedule book, copies of tenancy agreements and RM1,674 in cash believed to be proceeds from the activities.
Zakaria said the syndicate operated gambling activities discreetly from business premises under tight security.
The premises were only open to regular customers or people known to the operators, with various forms of gambling offered.
"The premises were also equipped with closed-circuit television cameras to monitor customers' movements or the presence of enforcement authorities.
"Access was controlled using locked magnetic steel doors operated from inside," he said.
The suspects are being investigated for various offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Immigration Regulations 1963.
All those detained were taken to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further action.
Zakaria said five local men were also issued notices requiring them to appear at the department's office to assist investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Volkswagen, Mercedes and BMW lose ground against global rivals
Article:
STUTTGART: Germany's three largest carmakers continued to lose ground to international rivals in the first half of the year, according to an analysis by consultancy EY, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
The combined revenue of Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz and BMW fell to around €284 billion (US$325 billion), a 2.9 per cent decrease from the previous year, EY said.
By comparison, the 19 other international automotive groups examined by EY increased their combined revenue by 3.6 per cent to just under €1.048 trillion (US$1.203 trillion).
According to the data, this marks the third consecutive first-half revenue decline for the German manufacturers.
The lag becomes even more apparent in the corporate ranking: according to EY, 15 carmakers recorded revenue increases, while the three German groups occupied places 16, 17 and 19.
Tesla achieved the strongest growth, followed by Suzuki and Geely.
The weakness of the German automotive industry is also reflected in profits: earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) of the German carmakers fell by 19 per cent to €13 billion (US$15 billion) in the first half of the year.
In absolute terms, VW, Mercedes-Benz and BMW remained well ahead of manufacturers from other countries.
However, according to the analysis, this was the lowest figure since the pandemic year of 2020. Performance also declined among manufacturers from China (minus 21.9 per cent) and Japan (minus 36.5 per cent).
Meanwhile, US manufacturers Ford, General Motors and Tesla recorded growth of 32.9 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals
Article:
NEW YORK: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are set to meet on Sunday to try to tee up potential agreements on AI, tariffs and critical minerals for a high-stakes Washington summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The meetings at JP Morgan Chase's headquarters in Manhattan, which also will include US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, are due to start at about 10:30 a.m. (1430 GMT) and are expected to run all day.
Key topics will be the status of a US-China trade truce that is set to expire on November 10, flows of Chinese rare-earth magnets and critical minerals that US officials say are insufficient and potential guard rails for artificial intelligence after reports of key security breaches involving AI models.
The most likely outcome, analysts say, would be for Washington and Beijing to agree on small steps to show they are continuing to avoid escalating tensions in a delicate trade relationship that has major consequences for the global economy.
"I think there will be some show of deliverables because of the fact that it's a presidential summit coming, but I don't feel like we're on the verge of some sort of breakthrough," said Anna Ashton, a longtime China trade analyst and founder of Ashton Intelligence. "I think status quo is probably both sides' general best expectation."
Many of the issues that He, Bessent and Greer will have to work through for Trump and Xi are holdovers from the two leaders' meeting in Beijing in May, including an effort on both sides to cut tariffs on non-strategic goods and Chinese pledges to increase purchases of US agricultural goods by US$17 billion a year and to purchase more than 200 Boeing aircraft.
The Bessent-He-Greer meeting follows a pattern set over the past 16 months, in which the three officials met in European and Asian cities to tee up potential agreements for Trump and Xi. These efforts included the November 2025 truce reached in Busan, South Korea, which capped US tariffs imposed during Trump's second term in office at about 20 per cent on Chinese goods after tit-for-tat escalation had brought them to triple-digit levels on both sides.
The US Supreme Court later struck down the Trump tariffs that were invoked under a national emergencies law, including duties related to fentanyl trafficking.
Trump's administration has been rebuilding them under new authorities, including restoring a 12.5 per cent tariff on Chinese goods over forced labor allegations. It is finalizing a separate tariff investigation aimed at curbing excess industrial capacity that it says is rampant in China.
Under that truce, China promised to restore the flow of critical minerals to US and global users. However, a senior US official told reporters on Friday that China's performance on that front "has not been up to par" and would be a topic for discussion ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
NEW TALKS ON AI
The Bessent-He discussions on AI are significant because the US and China are the two major forces driving development of advanced AI tools and the global adoption of the technology. Rare earths play a crucial role in the manufacturing of advanced semiconductor technology powering AI.
Bessent said on Friday he expects the discussions to cover "both open- and closed-weight models." Open-weight models are AI systems with publicly accessible core elements where users can download and fine-tune them for specific tasks.
Chinese open-weight models are becoming more popular with US companies because they can be cheaper than closed-weight AI tools such as those developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and other US companies.
"The United States remains the leader in AI. And we are open to discussions on avoiding shared risks and avoiding bifurcation of our two systems," Bessent said in a statement regarding the China talks.
Bessent has called for the US and China to agree on AI "guard rails" aimed at keeping powerful models out of the hands of malign non-state actors.
TARIFF REDUCTIONS, INVESTMENT
The US and China also agreed in May to launch discussions to reduce tariffs for non-strategic goods under a so-called "Board of Trade" mechanism along with a similar forum to deal with specific investment issues.
While the Trump administration has tightened restrictions on US companies investing in some industries in China, Reuters reported on Friday that it is working on rules that would likely allow US pharmaceutical firms to invest in promising Chinese drugs and strike licensing deals for them.
China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday that He would also lead a delegation of Chinese companies to the US that would participate in economic and trade consultations ahead of the summit.
The business delegation, which mirrors a group of US CEOs that Trump brought to Beijing in May, was announced as Trump expressed openness to Chinese automakers building US factories. US auto industry groups on Friday urged Trump to maintain an effective ban on Chinese vehicle sales in the US on national security grounds.

Title: Khaled: Malaysia will not send Malbatt peacekeepers to Yemen
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Malaysia will not send the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) peacekeeping force to Yemen as the country is currently involved in an active war and armed conflict.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malbatt peacekeepers are typically deployed to post-conflict areas rather than active war zones.
He said any decision to send peacekeeping forces remains subject to directives from the United Nations (UN) and is not made independently.
"Whatever decision we make is guided by the UN rather than done on our own. It is up to the UN to determine whether to deploy a peacekeeping force," he said.
[[nid:1536894]]
"In Lebanon, for example, our peacekeepers are deployed to ensure peace terms are respected. But in Yemen, there is an active war, and the UN has never sent forces to participate in a war," he told reporters after attending the Kota Tinggi Parliamentary Maulidur Rasul celebration at Dewan Besar Felda Air Tawar 2 here today.
Khaled noted that while Malaysia maintains diplomatic relations with the Yemeni government, the ongoing conflict involves Houthi forces in conflict with Saudi Arabia.
"There is the Yemeni government with which we have diplomatic relations, and there is another region occupied by the Houthi group. They are in conflict with Saudi Arabia, not Yemen as a whole," he said.
"We must understand that this is an active war. We cannot simply intervene in the middle of a war, as it will inevitably result in casualties," he added.

Title: As Iran war grinds on, Trump to face skeptical world leaders at UN
Article:
WHEN President Donald Trump addressed the United Nations a year ago, he touted the US bombing of Iran's nuclear sites just months earlier as "totally obliterating everything" and said he had brought peace between Israel and Iran.
Returning to the world body on Tuesday, Trump will face a deeply skeptical audience increasingly rattled by six months of war between US forces and an emboldened Iran, growing regional instability and a nuclear threat that has not disappeared despite his claims.
Though battered militarily and economically, Teheran has remained defiant, obstructing oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and in recent days gaining new leverage as its Houthi allies in Yemen tighten their grip on a Red Sea chokepoint, further spiking global energy prices.
The lightning advance by the Houthi militants has put Trump in an ever-tighter bind over the unpopular conflict, dealt a blow to US ally Saudi Arabia and exposed the limits of Washington's ability to protect its regional partners.
Most European and Asian allies have spurned Trump's demands for assistance in a conflict he launched without consulting them and which has had damaging fallout for their economies.
And with US gasoline prices high and his approval ratings low, Trump could pay a price in November's midterm elections when his Republican Party's control of Congress is at risk.
"We are seeing what happens when a president launches a war of choice without anticipating the unintended consequences," said Aaron David Miller, a former adviser on Middle East policy to Republican and Democratic administrations.
In Trump's speech to the annual gathering of heads of state and government in New York, he is likely again to frame as a victory a military campaign he promised would be over in weeks.
The conflict has instead hardened into an uneasy stalemate that has failed to achieve Trump's shifting goals while depleting the Pentagon's missile stockpiles.
Trump's problems have only deepened since Houthi fighters overcame Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces, sweeping down the Red Sea coast and seizing islands at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping corridor that allows Iran to further threaten global oil supplies.
In response to Reuters' questions, a senior Trump administration official said the US is focused on security interests such as ensuring freedom of navigation in the Red Sea "while empowering our regional partners to take the lead in managing and resolving regional security challenges."
Iran took up only a small portion of Trump's speech at last year's UN General Assembly.
He recounted how, three months before, he had sent B-2 bombers to drop 30,000-pound bombs that "demolished" Teheran's uranium enrichment capacity. However, experts determined the strikes had only seriously set back the programme.
"No other country on Earth could have done what we did," Trump said.
The US president – who campaigned on a vow to avoid foreign military entanglements - also presented himself as a peacemaker, repeating claims to have ended conflicts around the world, including a 12-day war between Israel and Iran in 2025, and again insisted he should receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
Events since then stand in contrast to his remarks.
Trump joined Israel in striking Iran on Feb 28, citing what he said was an imminent nuclear threat to the US. Experts have disputed his claim that Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon, which Teheran has always denied seeking.
But Trump underestimated Iran's resilience, analysts say. Despite airstrikes that killed many of Iran's top leaders, it has hit back at Gulf neighbours and the US bases they host.
At the same time, Iran has retained a stockpile of near-weapons-grade highly enriched uranium believed buried by the US strikes in June 2025.
White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said Trump alone had "possessed the courage" to confront Iran over its nuclear programme, that he had achieved all his objectives and Iran's economy was being crippled by stepped-up sanctions and a US maritime blockade.
Trump, meanwhile, has rebuffed Saudi pleas for direct military intervention against the Houthis, who agreed to a ceasefire with the US last year.
This has dented confidence about US security guarantees among Gulf states, whose doubts had already been fed by Trump's decision to go to war over their objections, analysts say.
He plans to meet Gulf leaders on the UN sidelines next week, Axios reported.
The dilemma for Trump is that while the US can ill afford to have the Houthis close a second major shipping corridor, he is reluctant to undertake a dangerous new mission for a US military stretched by the fighting against Iran.
US officials met the Houthis last weekend in Oman, where the group said that while it was targeting Saudi shipping it had no intention of attacking American vessels, according to five people familiar with the matter.
"The US clearly has (military) capacity challenges but even so the cost of inaction here is likely to intensify tensions among Gulf allies," said Jonathan Panikoff, a former deputy national intelligence officer on the Middle East.
The Houthis' sudden re-emergence as a regional threat has further complicated Trump's efforts to find a way out of the conflict.
With the war grinding on in a seventh month, the US is mired in a battle of attrition while Trump tries to intensify economic pressure on Teheran.
Trump, who has offered shifting timelines, told reporters on Wednesday that "hopefully we are towards the end."
But analysts warn that the conflict is likely to drag on well past the midterm elections.
"Iran isn't about to let him off the hook here while they have so much leverage to damage him in the midterms and make him a lame duck," Brett Erickson, a geopolitical analyst and managing principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, wrote on X.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Locked grille foils son's desperate attempt to save mother in fatal Tambun fire
Article:
IPOH: A desperate son reached through smoke and held his mother's hand after hearing her screams, but a locked grille prevented him from pulling her to safety during a fire that killed three family members at Taman Desa Tambun early today.
Raja Muhammad Syukri Raja Ahmad, 30, climbed to the upper floor from the back of the house after learning that his parents, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, and Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, were trapped inside.
The blaze also claimed the life of his nephew, Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, 18, who had lived with his grandparents since childhood.
His brother, Raja Ikhwan Hadi, 47, said Syukri managed to reach their mother's hand but could not pull her out.
"He managed to hold my mother's hand, but he could not get her out because the grille was locked.
"He told her to move towards the bathroom, but he eventually had to climb back down," he said when met at the scene.
Raja Ikhwan, who was sleeping on the front porch when the fire broke out, was awakened by shouts for help and breaking glass.
"At first, I heard someone shouting for help, but I did not think much of it. Then I heard glass breaking and immediately got up. I heard the cries again and ran outside.
"I thought the voice came from a neighbour's house, but when I looked up, I realised it was my own house," he said, adding that the screams came from Nik Abdurrahman.
Raja Ikhwan and several others rushed inside and found flames at the staircase.
He attempted to douse the fire with a garden hose, but it was too short to reach the flames.
He then ran outside to seek help from neighbours. Syukri, who was at a neighbour's house nearby, rushed over and attempted to reach their parents from the back.
However, Syukri could only reach their mother's hand before the locked grille forced him to retreat.
A friend later managed to enter through the kitchen after breaking down the door, while neighbours helped remove a gas cylinder from the premises.
He said they later informed firefighters that his father was still inside the bathroom.
"The smoke was already very thick. The fire spread very quickly before the firefighters arrived," he said.
He explained that he regularly slept on the porch when returning late to avoid disturbing his elderly parents.
Before going to sleep, his mother had gone outside to switch off the lights and mentioned feeling uneasy.
"Before I went to sleep, my mother said she felt that something was wrong. She looked worried and said she had a feeling that something was going to happen. Then she said, 'Oh, it's nothing'," Raja Ikhwan said.
He added that six people reside in the home, but two family members were away when the fire occurred.
Meanwhile, Nik Abdurrahman's father, Helal Zamri, 37, said he rushed to the scene from his home in Manjoi at 5am after being informed of the incident.
"When I arrived, I saw the fire still burning. We could only wait for the rescue and recovery process. The bodies were brought out at 8am.
"Nik had lived with my parents-in-law since he was a child. All three of them did not survive. We are now waiting for the forensic examination results from Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital," he said, adding that he accepted the loss.
He added that his son was a cheerful person and, although he could sometimes be serious, he was generally happy.
"He did not really like being around many people.
However, when he was with us, his friends or while working, he was fine," he said.

Title: Anwar conveys condolences to family of Tambun fire victims, provides immediate aid
Article:
IPOH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has conveyed his condolences to the family of three victims killed in a house fire here, instructing his service centre to render immediate assistance to ease their burden.
The special officer to the Tambun member of parliament, Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri, said Anwar was informed of the tragedy and instructed the service centre to provide all required support.
"He conveyed his condolences to the family and directed us at the service centre to provide all possible assistance to ease their burden," he told reporters at the scene in Taman Desa Tambun today.
Hairul Amir, who is also the Perak PKR chairman, said the service centre had today handed the family RM5,000 in immediate aid.
He said the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) would conduct an assessment tomorrow to determine the extent of further assistance required, including possible repairs to the fire-damaged house.
"The ICU will come to conduct an assessment tomorrow, and we will see how we can help with the repairs. There may also be other forms of assistance," he said.
He said temporary accommodation could also be arranged if required, as repairing the house could take some time.
"We will see whether they need help with accommodation. We will try to arrange temporary accommodation, perhaps by helping with the rental costs first.
"Looking at the condition of the house, it may take quite a long time to repair, so the service centre may help provide them with a place to stay while the repairs are carried out," he said.
Hairul Amir said the service centre would also discuss possible counselling and other support with the Social Welfare Department and relevant agencies.
"We will discuss this tomorrow and see what assistance is appropriate for the family, who have been affected by the loss of three family members," he said.
On funeral arrangements, he said the service centre would continue to support the family until all matters were settled.
He said family members were expected to go to the hospital this afternoon for identification and forensic procedures, while the burial was expected to take place tomorrow.
"We will do our best to assist them until everything is completed," he said.
Earlier, it was reported that three family members were killed while another survived after a
fire destroyed their two-storey terrace house
at Taman Desa Tambun here.
The dead were identified as Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, and Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, 18. The sole survivor was identified as Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad, 47.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received an emergency call about the fire at 4am.

Title: White House press group demands Trump immediately lift reporters ban
Article:
WASHINGTON: An association representing hundreds of journalists who cover the White House demanded Saturday the restoration of access for banned colleagues, calling the removal unconstitutional.
"Today's action revoking access for journalists from CNN, POLITICO, and MSNOW violates the First Amendment," the White House Correspondents' Association said, urging the Trump administration "to immediately restore our colleagues' access."
They are expected to take the bans to court to regain access to the White House, fighting back as Trump expands his battle against mainstream news outlets that he detests and routinely slams as crooked.
"The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded with our tax dollars," MS NOW, formerly known as MSNBC, said Saturday on X.
CNN said it has "a right under the US Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government, and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right."
The White House declined to issue any new statements on the matter on Saturday, referring AFP to Trump's comments Friday announcing the bans.
An association representing hundreds of journalists who cover the White House called the ban a violation of the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which enshrines press freedom, and called for immediate restoration of access for banned colleagues.
"Courts have repeatedly held that once the White House provides access to journalists, it cannot deny that access arbitrarily or based on the content of their reporting," the White House Correspondent's Association (WHCA) said.
MS NOW White House correspondent Akayla Gardner described how her access badge did not work Saturday when she tried to go through her usual security checkpoint.
"There was a red beeping light and so the officer asked me to hand over my badge," she said in an on-air play-by-play of the incident.
Betsy Klein of CNN gave a similar account of being unable to enter the White House grounds as she normally does every day.
"There was a group of cameras waiting outside that gate to watch me walk in," she told her network.
Cheyenne Haslett of Politico was also denied entry and the Secret Service confiscated her access pass, editor-in-chief Jonathan Greenberger said in a note sent to AFP.
Trump did not detail what prompted the ban but said "media Outlets shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States."
The 80-year-old Republican -- who has long had a fiery relationship with the mainstream media -- warned Friday that other outlets could face a similar fate but did not say which ones.
Both of Trump's White House terms have seen him lash out repeatedly at media whose coverage displeases him.
He has filed multiple defamation suits against news outlets, attacked the press on Truth Social and verbally assaulted several reporters, notably women, including CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins.
But it is rare for US presidents to outright bar news outlets from the White House -- although Trump in his first term banned CNN reporter Jim Acosta, an action which a court subsequently overturned.
Last year, Trump barred The Associated Press from some events because of the news agency's decision to continue using the term "Gulf of Mexico" -- and not the "Gulf of America" as decreed by Trump.
His administration has also put stricter controls on journalists, including taking control of which outlets can cover events as part of the "pool" admitted to small spaces such as the Oval Office and Air Force One.
Trump's surprise announcement on Friday comes at a time when his approval ratings are at record lows and his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in November's midterm elections.
The war in Iran and rising prices, particularly at the gas pump, are among the factors that have contributed to his sinking political fortunes.

Title: Sabah MACC nabs two civil servants over RM30,000 false claims
Article:
LAHAD DATU: The Sabah Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested two civil servants for allegedly submitting false claims amounting to nearly RM30,000.
The claims involved allowances for security patrol and disaster monitoring duties allegedly committed between 2022 and 2023.
The two male suspects, in their 30s and 40s, were detained at 10am on Thursday after giving their statements at the Lahad Datu MACC branch office.
Initial investigations revealed that both suspects allegedly conspired to commit the offense.
Sabah MACC director Datuk Mohd Fuad Bee Basrah confirmed the arrests when contacted.
"The case is being investigated under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009, and both suspects will be charged at the Tawau Special Corruption Court on Sept 24," he said.

Title: Families demand justice after deaths of 37 miners in detention
Article:
MINNA, Nigeria: Families of some of the people who died in a Nigerian paramilitary civil defence force holding cell, on Saturday demanded justice as government appointed an independent panel to probe the deaths.
Thirty-seven young men were found dead inside a crowded cell in Minna, the capital of central Niger state, on Thursday after their arrest on suspicion of illegal goldmining by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).
Survivors recounted being crammed in the cell with poor ventilation, and one said a substance that stung their throats and noses was sprayed into the cell before the door was slammed shut.
They said their calls for help were ignored.
The deaths triggered violent protests on the streets of Minna city, the capital of mineral-rich Niger state, and police fired shots to disperse the protesters.
Nigeria's government has appointed a 10-member independent panel to investigate the deaths of 37 people in a paramilitary civil defence force holding cell, the interior ministry said Saturday.
Adamu Idris, 27, whose brother was among the dead told AFP he expects government "to give us justice."
He warned: "If the government does not take decisive action, we will continue the protest.
"They should be ready to continue killing us, and it is better that we all die."
Musa Aliyu, 52, who lost two sons in detention wants the disaster "thoroughly" investigated to "give justice to our children."
Tensions were stoked at the news of the deaths and people poured out into the streets protesting and damaging government property.
Gunshots were heard in the city as police responded with fire to disperse the protesters, but it was not clear whether they fired anti-riot pellets or live ammunition.
But one man said he was shot while walking on the streets on his way from attending the funeral of one of the miners.
"I heard gunshots. I quickly ducked and next thing I was unconscious, I was shot. I fell into the gutter," 24-year-old Allamin Adamu, said from his hospital bed.
President Bola Tinubu on Friday ordered an urgent, "full and transparent investigation" over Thursday's deaths.
He said he would not tolerate deaths caused by "official negligence, abuse, dereliction of duty."
The panel includes a retired senior state intelligence officer, a medical expert, a human rights activist and a miners' association.
It has two weeks to finalise investigations and submit its report.
Twenty NSCDC officers and guards who were involved in the arrests and detention of the miners had been suspended, along with their boss.
Niger state, more than twice the size of Belgium, is rich in minerals and attracts thousands of artisanal miners – most of them lured by the hope of striking gold.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Government has explained Najib's conditional pardon, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil stressed that the conditional pardon granted to Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve his remaining sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, is the sole prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim.
He said the matter had been clarified by the Prime Minister's Department's Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) in an official statement.
"This decision is based on Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, which outlines the royal prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"Pakatan Harapan issued a statement last week, and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, who represents the government on the Pardons Board, has also issued a statement.
"In fact, the prime minister stated yesterday that the decision to grant the conditional pardon rests with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and was executed by the Pardons Board.
"I believe those statements are sufficient," he told reporters after launching the Communications Ministry's 2025 Madani Adopted Village at the Surau Kampung Tebat Kering compound here today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, Kuala Pilah District Council president Nawal Mohamed Amin, and senior ministry officials.
Fahmi was responding to calls from various quarters for the government to publicly clarify the conditional pardon decision following mixed reactions from the public.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said residents of Kampung Tebat Kering now enjoy safer and more comfortable infrastructure built using Industrialised Building System (IBS) technology under the ministry's Madani Adopted Village project.
He said the old, dilapidated surau was demolished and replaced with a new, sturdy building featuring safe electrical wiring that complies with safety standards.
"IBS allows the structure to be completed in a short timeframe, accelerating the handover of the facility for residents' daily use," he said.
He added that the ministry also upgraded the Kampung Bukit Temensu and Kampung Tebat community halls, involving an allocation of nearly RM1 million, to serve as centres for community bonding and social activities.
